plugins.name: agent-memory

L1 to L2 needs three distinct sessions spanning two distinct calendar days (a stated claim needs two; a verified claim is the only single-observation path); L2 to L3 needs two projects and thirty days. Two gates refuse rather than guess: a claim altered by the redaction pass never promotes on evidence alone, and a contradicted claim freezes until a human resolves it. Three hooks run the loop unattended and every one fails open. Nothing reaches a committed CLAUDE.md without an explicit human adopt. Ships 5 stdlib scripts, 3 hooks, a cs-memory-curator agent, /cs-memory, a JSON schema, and a 69-check validator. Concept from TencentCloud/TencentDB-Agent-Memory (MIT); no upstream code included.

Ships a glossary, a patterns file with 16 techniques, a decision cheatsheet with thresholds, a cs-spinning-up-deep-rl agent and /cs-spinning-up-deep-rl. Structured study notes, not a reproduction of the source.

Four stdlib tools make it executable — a prerequisite-closed reading-path planner that refuses goals the book does not cover, a training diagnostic running Chapter 11's rules in priority order so a NaN is never reported as overfitting, a capacity planner that ranks 'shrink the model' last when overparameterized, and a parameter/FLOP/activation-memory calculator that refuses a stack whose shapes do not connect. A companion, not a compilation: the book is copyrighted, so nothing here reproduces its text.

Ships cs-eval-gatekeeper agent, /cs-agent-evals and /cs-eval-gate commands, 3 references, and a CI job example.

Secrets are always redacted. A UserPromptSubmit hook gives the agent this session's transcript path when a prompt asks about past work. Ships cs-run-forensics agent, /cs-run-forensics and /cs-check-claims commands and 3 cited references.

plugins.name: i18n-localization

Ships cs-claude-code-rollout agent, /cs-claude-rollout and /cs-claude-settings-lint commands, 3 references, a baseline managed-settings policy and a four-phase rollout plan.

plugins.name: month-end-close

plugins.name: codex-hud

plugins.name: magic-cc-codex-worker
plugins.description: Turns OpenAI Codex into a pool of parallel agent workers inside Claude Code. Each worker runs in its own git worktree so parallel edits don't collide. Resumable sessions via Codex's native thread_id, dual-model PR review with materialized detached worktree, and role-based specialization (implementer/reviewer/planner/generic).

plugins.name: vibe-prospecting
plugins.description: Power your chat with live B2B data to create lead lists, research companies, enrich contacts, personalize outreach, and inspect business signals, tech stacks, events, and website changes. 150M+ businesses and 800M+ professionals via the Explorium MCP.

plugins.name: backlogd
plugins.description: Turn Claude Code into a problem-driven scrum team. You file problems as Linear issues; an agent team runs the empirical Scrum loop (scope, solve, review, adapt) and owns the solutions. An independent reviewer gates every increment against its acceptance criteria, the Definition of Done, and a standards corpus. Runs on your Claude subscription via the official Linear MCP over OAuth — no API keys.

plugins.name: kegg-mcp-server
plugins.description: Query the KEGG bioinformatics database — pathways, genes, compounds, drugs, enzymes, diseases, reactions, and more via 34 read-only MCP tools. No API key required.

plugins.name: claude-wayfinder
plugins.description: Helps Claude make deterministic, auditable choices about which agent and skills to use for a given task — replacing prose-scanning agent/skill selection with a typed scoring kernel that returns one of seven typed decisions with confidence, rationale, and alternatives.

plugins.name: claude-prospector
plugins.description: Claude Code efficiency and hygiene toolkit. Surfaces token spend across the 5h / 7d / Sonnet-7d billing windows with per-model / per-agent / per-skill attribution, and audits your effective Claude Code configuration (custom + plugin agents and skills) for overlap and conflicts. Ships an interactive dashboard, a conversational usage-analysis skill, and a structured config-audit skill.

plugins.name: claude-github-tools
plugins.description: GitHub workflow skills for Claude Code - issue creation, PR review triage, backlog summaries/quick-wins, release status, and GitHub Actions authoring. Seven skills; three pure-LLM, four script-backed via an auto-materialized plugin venv.

plugins.name: ultracost
plugins.description: Per-stage model routing + pre-flight cost gate for Claude Code ultracode dynamic workflows. Pins an explicit model + effort on every agent() subagent stage, estimates cost before launch, and ships a static guard + PreToolUse gate that flag stages which would silently inherit the session's Opus model. Zero dependencies, no telemetry, MIT.

plugins.name: forge
plugins.description: Full-lifecycle SDLC orchestrator: a 12-stage pipeline (SRS, architecture, spec, plan, build, eval, deploy, monitor, release) driven by specialized agents, persistent cross-session memory, auto-reflection, gate enforcement, and semantic skill mining that proposes new skills from recurring workflows.

plugins.name: codex-orchestrator
plugins.description: Orchestrate OpenAI Codex from Claude through supervised checkpoint slices, server-enforced quality gates, persistent plans and hypotheses, worktree isolation, and per-task model and effort control.

plugins.name: claude-md-kit
plugins.description: Scaffold and audit CLAUDE.md files from inside Claude Code: /claude-md-new builds one from battle-tested templates using your repo's real commands; /claude-md-audit grades an existing one and returns worst-first fixes.

plugins.name: fabler-relay
plugins.description: Human-in-the-loop request queue for autonomous agents: file a blocker (account creation, CAPTCHA-gated step, purchase approval) to a human operator via MCP, poll for the result, keep working. Talks to your own self-hosted Cloudflare Worker.

plugins.name: fabler-x402-tools
plugins.description: Nine MCP tools for security audits, web scraping, OG rendering, and funding spreads. Default setup is inspect-only and requires no wallet key. Optional x402 auto-payment requires X402_BUYER_PRIVATE_KEY; use only a dedicated low-balance wallet funded with what you are willing to spend.

plugins.name: travel-agent-skill
plugins.description: 私人旅行管家 · Travel Agent — 在 Claude Code 中一句话规划完整旅行。AI 自动联网查实时车次、景点、美食信息，输出闭环行程并生成 HTML 攻略。每个行程项带 12306/携程/大众点评/高德/小红书一键跳转。

plugins.name: chamnan
plugins.description: Makes a repository know itself and preserve the engineering context built while you work with it, so an agent stops rediscovering both. An architecture index and an impact map instead of scanning files; work state, session records and the decisions behind them instead of losing context between sessions; the procedures, tools and workflows you keep re-deriving. Everything is repository-local markdown, committed beside the code. For long-lived repos you revisit, not one-off scripts.

plugins.name: cohesivity
plugins.description: cohesivity.ai offers free agent native backend services. Anonymous account (no-signup) to get started through MCP or API. Hosting, postgres, email, storage, containers, LLMs, voice and third-party APIs. Includes free tiers and 5 USD/mo in AI and Search credits. topups through x402.

plugins.name: usage-limits
plugins.description: Reads how much of your 5-hour and weekly Claude Code limit is left, converts it into turns of headroom rather than a percentage, and plans the work to fit inside it. Detects plan tier, splits spend by model and project, and adds a status line.

plugins.name: computer-use
plugins.description: Codex-style computer use for Claude Code. Drives Windows and macOS apps through the accessibility tree instead of screenshots, so it targets exactly, survives display scaling, and costs about 20x fewer tokens. It can also work on the same desktop while you keep working, telling your input apart from its own.

plugins.name: suede-skills
plugins.description: 74 skills for Claude Code and Codex. A build DAG researches your repo, fans out disjoint lanes, and refutes its own review before anything lands. A blunt A-F ship grade blocks the bad merge instead of complimenting it. The same folder designs the page, writes the copy, and ships native iOS and Android builds.

plugins.name: phaneslight
plugins.description: Multi-agent orchestration and project-memory system for Claude Code. One command turns a repository into a wired multi-agent environment: a project-specific agent roster, a documentation and session-summary tree, a tested script library, and enforcement hooks that hold size and stamp discipline at the harness layer. Re-runnable, so the setup grows with the codebase.

plugins.name: curviate
plugins.description: Agent skills for driving LinkedIn work through the Curviate CLI: profiles and companies, search, inbox and messaging, posts and comments, network, job postings, and the Sales Navigator and Recruiter surfaces.

plugins.name: isitdone
plugins.description: Don't let Claude say "done" until the tests actually pass. A Stop hook runs the repository's real test, typecheck and lint commands and blocks the turn until they pass; a PostToolUse hook warns when an edit weakened a test; a skill teaches Claude to verify before claiming completion. No LLM calls, no network.

plugins.name: yylo-skills
plugins.description: Reusable agent skills maintained by YYLO. The canonical, independently versioned source for skills used by YYLO CLI and YYLO Ledger: ledger task management, wiki, workflow and artifact records, project understanding, planning, and the Ralph execution loop.

plugins.name: traderspy-mcp
plugins.description: TraderSpy — Read-only smart money tracking, AI trading signals, and elite trader leaderboard for crypto futures. Track whale positions across Binance, Hyperliquid, Bybit, and OKX. No order or withdrawal tools.

plugins.name: papi
plugins.description: Persistent project management inside your AI coding tool. PAPI turns a plan into a cycle of scoped tasks, hands each one to your agent with a build spec, records what actually happened, and keeps every decision alive across sessions — so a new session resumes where the last one stopped instead of starting from nothing. Connects to the hosted PAPI server over OAuth; nothing runs locally.

plugins.name: active-memory
plugins.description: Switch to a fresh Claude chat without losing a single rule, correction or number. /amhandoff writes a complete handoff file, and a code word plus checkpoints warn you when it is time to switch.

plugins.name: carrick
plugins.description: Claude Code plugin for Carrick, which indexes TypeScript codebases across service and repository boundaries. After each edit it adds the file's routes, calls, and cross-service type mismatches to the session, and it registers Carrick's language server. It pairs with the Carrick MCP server, which lets agents search functions by intent rather than name.

plugins.name: production-fast-api-template
plugins.description: Production-ready standards for a scalable, unified FastAPI + RAG + Agentic AI backend on AWS ECS Fargate: project structure, async execution, Pydantic and structured outputs, API conventions, guardrails, AI evaluation (DeepEval, Ragas), API security and LLM/agent security.

plugins.name: apmzoom-dongdaemun
plugins.description: Search Dongdaemun (Seoul) wholesale fashion with apMZoomAI: items, new arrivals and stalls by building and floor, with links back to apMZoomAI. A read-only remote MCP server plus a sourcing skill; no prices or contact details.

plugins.name: feedbacks
plugins.description: Read visual website feedback, marked screenshots, recordings and team discussion through a scoped MCP connection. Includes review-feedback and manage-feedbacks-context skills. Requires a Feedbacks server, Node 22.12+ or 24 and Git.

plugins.name: postel
plugins.description: Find what's going viral in your niche, write your version in your own voice, and schedule it to X, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Mastodon, YouTube and TikTok through your Postel account. A remote MCP server (OAuth) plus a writing skill.

plugins.name: symbioza
plugins.description: Run a GPU job under a hard dollar cap and collect the files it writes.

plugins.name: publish-fun
plugins.description: Submit, revise and track research papers at Publish.fun, an AI-reviewed research journal, and cite published papers. Bundles the journal's remote MCP server and its agent skill. Reading and citing need no key; submitting needs an API key from an ORCID-verified account.

plugins.name: ti-edgeai-skills
plugins.description: Train, compile, deploy and profile neural networks on Texas Instruments Edge AI processors (C7x/MMA with TIDL: TDA4VM, AM68A, AM69A, AM67A, AM62A). Five skills cover TIDL compilation and int8 calibration in Docker, host-vs-board output checks, edgeai-gst-apps configs and per-layer profiling. Asks before any board-state change.

plugins.name: watch-for-me
plugins.description: Watch any video (YouTube, X, Instagram, TikTok, local files) on-device: local speech transcription plus keyframes read by your agent, several videos in parallel.

plugins.name: voicemoat-skills
plugins.description: Twenty-six free skills for writing on LinkedIn and Twitter: write in your voice, audit a draft before you publish, draft comments, fix opening lines and endings, read your numbers and plan the week. They need no account; connecting VoiceMoat (Pro or Enterprise) adds a voice profile trained on your own published posts and a Voice Match score.

plugins.name: nibbl
plugins.description: A tamagotchi-style pixel pet in a band above the prompt, built on function hooks. It reacts to tool calls, passing checks and commits, and adds a /nibbl command. Uses zero model tokens; syncs event types and times plus a hashed machine id to getnibbl.pages.dev.

plugins.name: bettercallgpt
plugins.description: Put this Claude Code session on a full-duplex voice call (Azure GPT Realtime or GPT-Live, macOS): talk while it codes, interrupt anytime, hear results read back. Voice never approves permission prompts; they stay on the keyboard.

plugins.name: midpoint-card-prices
plugins.description: Trading card market prices and grading ROI through one remote MCP server. Raw and graded prices for 1.5M+ Pokémon, Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Lorcana and sports cards, PSA 9 and PSA 10 premiums, net profit after grading fees, price history, 30-day movers and priced set checklists. Read-only, no account, no API key.

plugins.name: kumi
plugins.description: A coordinated engineering team of named AI specialists that remembers your project between sessions. Call yui to route work, or call any specialist directly: Go (jaan, siim, mart), Angular (liis, kadi, tiiu), iOS (ren, shu, ryo), Python (eero, anu, ivo), React (noa, rui, aki), SQL (saku), NoSQL (remo), architecture for any stack (kai), process management (enn), and DevOps/infra (sora). Each ships as both a skill and a subagent. Bundled hooks capture finished work when a session ends and say at the next session start that saved work exists, and record per-session and per-agent token and time usage. Every specialist follows the same discipline: read context first, make the smallest correct change, verify.

plugins.name: clawd-actor
plugins.description: While Claude works, Clawd (Claude Code's mascot) acts out the spinner's -ing word and the running tool on a little stage above the prompt: 26 animated scenes, wandering the band, changing scene every 30 seconds on long turns.

plugins.name: figma-maxxing
plugins.description: Agent skills for real Figma files: Plugin API gotchas, checks before and after every write, comments to verified fixes, handoff gate.

plugins.name: bestax
plugins.description: Build with Bestax, React components for Bulma v1. Seven Agent Skills for forms, layouts, theming, icons, custom components, CSS size and migration from Bulma classes or older React Bulma libraries, plus the bestax-mcp server, which answers questions about components, props, examples and CSS variables from a bundled index. Local stdio server, exact npm pin, no telemetry.

plugins.name: equibles
plugins.description: US stock market research through the hosted Equibles MCP server: SEC filings with full-text search, XBRL financial statements, earnings call transcripts, insider and congressional trades, 13F institutional holdings, short interest, end-of-day prices, option chains and macroeconomic data. Sign in over OAuth from /mcp; free tier of 100 requests a day, no credit card.

plugins.name: claude-usage
plugins.description: Lets Claude check its own claude.ai plan quota: percent used of the session and weekly limits (including per-model weekly limits), when each resets, and where usage is on pace to be at reset. One skill and a short Python script that reads Claude Code's stored login token and calls the same usage endpoint as /usage. Claude Code only; no hooks, MCP servers, or telemetry.

plugins.name: herdr-toolkit
plugins.description: One skill for running Claude Code on Herdr, the terminal agent multiplexer. spawn-session starts a named, detached Claude Code Remote Control session for any project directory in its own Herdr pane, so it appears in the Claude mobile app, and confirms on the pane screen that each prompt landed.

plugins.name: ask-human-expert
plugins.description: Ask real executives, operators and domain experts a question through Instant Expert and get a written or voice answer or a short call. It finds people by description or reaches a named person, and the user approves every live order. Starts in a free test mode with no account; you pay only if someone answers.

plugins.name: auten
plugins.description: Computer use for Claude Code: click, type and read the screen on your Mac, Windows or Linux computer and your Android phone over USB (beta), even in apps with no API. Reads the accessibility tree, types saved passwords locally, and asks before anything irreversible. Free plan 30 minutes of runtime a month.

plugins.name: memory-loop
plugins.description: A lifecycle for Claude Code native file-based memory: a save gate that gives each memory a tier and an expiry, a sweep that archives expired memories instead of deleting them, a consolidation pass that merges duplicates and resolves contradictions only after you confirm, and a correction-signal hook that feeds an always-loaded HABITS.md capped at 8000 bytes / 24 rules, enforced at write time. Local-only.

plugins.name: lnpl
plugins.description: Authoring and verification for LNPL, the language of the linkly LLM-native platform (declare entities, services and workflows; the compiler lowers them to a semantic IR that runs on an interpreter or compiles through MLIR to a native binary). LNPL's verb vocabulary is closed and absent from model training data, so a plausible word compiles into a step that silently does nothing. The plugin routes Claude to the lexicon generated from the compiler's own tables, surfaces lnpl compile diagnostics on every save, offers an independent reviewer subagent, derives spec cases, and gates completion on evidence.

plugins.name: ngx-json-render
plugins.description: Two skills for generative UI in Angular with ngx-json-render, the Angular renderer for Vercel's json-render: define a component catalog and registry, render model-written JSON specs with <json-render>, stream them with signals, check specs and test components, and use the ready Angular Material catalog.

plugins.name: render-policy
plugins.description: Two skills for rendering agent output safely: replace innerHTML with render-policy's sanitize-into-a-fragment renderers for plain DOM, React and Angular, with image, link and host policies, streaming and ESLint rules; and lint the CSP and tool metadata an MCP App declares before you publish it.

plugins.name: skyvern
plugins.description: Browser automation in Claude Code through Skyvern Cloud: open pages, fill forms, extract structured data, take screenshots, and run repeatable workflows. Sign in with OAuth from /mcp. Runs can use Skyvern credits.

plugins.name: baizhi-agent-toolkit
plugins.description: Connect Baizhi Agent Toolkit through an authenticated remote MCP server, with an optional skill for bounded research and source verification. Requires a Baizhi account and API key; service usage may incur charges.

plugins.name: cc-aws-keepalive
plugins.description: Keeps Claude Code sessions on AWS Bedrock alive through credential expiry. Scripts for awsCredentialExport and awsAuthRefresh, added to settings.json by hand, read fresh credentials from ~/.aws/credentials and can re-run your login. A UserPromptSubmit hook warns when expiry is near or past. Works with saml2aws, gimme-aws-creds, aws-google-auth and any tool that writes to ~/.aws/credentials.

plugins.name: ultramod
plugins.description: All-in-one mod pack for Claude Code: a usage limits and context HUD, a guard with undo for rm -rf and git reset --hard, .env and secret protection, and a receipt for every turn. Ten mods in one plugin; needs Claude Code 2.1.287 or later.

plugins.name: reevesagents
plugins.description: Lets Claude Code start other AI coding CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, Qwen, OpenCode) in their own tmux windows, send them prompts, read their output and stop them, through the reevesagents MCP server. Ships one skill and the MCP config; needs the reevesagents npm package and tmux.

plugins.name: convika
plugins.description: Publish a page Claude wrote, or an HTML file in your repo, at a convika.com address or on your own domain. Convika keeps signups from the page's form and counts visits, traffic sources, and button clicks. Sign-in is OAuth in the browser, so Claude never holds an API key. The publish-page skill shows a private preview and asks before it publishes.

plugins.name: korean-law
plugins.description: Search and read Korean law through the official Ministry of Government Legislation (법제처) Open API: statutes, precedents, administrative rules, local ordinances, treaties and legal interpretations. Also checks legal citations in Claude's answers against the source for existence and content. Runs the korean-law-mcp MCP server via npx and needs a free 법제처 API key (LAW_OC), entered at install.

plugins.name: kordoc
plugins.description: Read, create, fill, patch and compare Korean documents in Claude. One skill that runs the kordoc CLI via npx to convert HWP 3.x/5.x, HWPX, HWPML, PDF, DOCX and XLS/XLSX files to Markdown, fill form templates while keeping their formatting, and generate HWPX documents from Markdown with Korean government document presets. No Hancom Office needed.

plugins.name: harness-scope
plugins.description: A Claude Code mod that turns global skills, agents, instruction files (CLAUDE.md and rules) and tools on or off per repo through named profiles. A repo picks a profile with a one-line .claude/harness-scope.json; repos without the file are unchanged. It only reads: no file writes, network requests, child processes or model calls.

plugins.name: guardrails
plugins.description: PreToolUse Bash guard for Claude Code that still holds under --dangerously-skip-permissions. Blocks pipe-to-shell installs, disk wipes and fork bombs; asks before rm -rf, force-push, git reset --hard, DROP/TRUNCATE, kubectl delete, cloud deletes and secret-file reads. 15 rules, each off/ask/block; a project's own config can only tighten them, loosening comes only from your config outside the project. Plus a PostToolUse audit log with secrets redacted and /guardrails:self-test to see every decision without running anything.

plugins.name: dev-loop
plugins.description: Multi-agent orchestration grounded in an LLM wiki. /dev-loop:orchestrate splits one goal into a dependency graph of parallel Claude Code sessions, each in its own worktree, and supervises them natively on Orca (a tracked Task + Dispatch per phase, pushed worker_done / question / escalation events instead of polling, stall detection; raw tmux fallback). Every plan decision must cite a page in a bundled best-practice wiki of 400+ pages across 10 domains, checked by machine gates and a fresh-context plan reviewer. Insights from your sessions are queued and turned into reviewed wiki PRs when you run /dev-loop:knowledge-flush (automatic flushing is opt-in and never bypasses permission checks).

plugins.name: lnpl-mcp
plugins.description: The LNPL compiler (linkly LLM-native platform) as MCP tools instead of a shell command. lnpl compile writes diagnostics to stderr and exits 0, so a caller that checks the exit code misses every warning, and an unknown-verb warning means a step that does nothing at runtime. lnpl_compile, lnpl_spec and lnpl_kb_route return diagnostics, spec results and knowledge-base routes as structured records, calling the compiler in-process with no PATH lookup. The compiler is loaded only from a path you configure (LNPL_IMPL_PATH) or an installed package, never from the project directory.

plugins.name: kernel-development-skills
plugins.description: Kernel Field Guide: Linux kernel development the way experienced kernel engineers work: driver code and teardown order, devicetree bindings and DTS, Kconfig, debugging by symptom, KUnit and kselftest, patch review and submission, regressions and bot reports, and stable, LTS, and vendor kernel trees.

plugins.name: looot
plugins.description: Search, price and run 2,500+ data API endpoints (work emails, company and people search, Google results, web pages) with one prepaid balance. The agent sees the price before a call runs, and a failed call costs nothing. Remote MCP server with browser sign-in plus one skill.

plugins.name: show-receipts
plugins.description: Stop hook for Claude Code and Codex. When the agent ends with "all tests pass", "the build succeeds" or "lint is clean", it checks the session transcript for a matching command that ran after the last edit and exited 0, and blocks the stop if there isn't one. One file of standard-library Python, no LLM, no network.

plugins.name: uxkin
plugins.description: Real UI, not AI slop. The free no-ui-slop and uxkin-research skills (work with no account), plus the optional UXKIN MCP server for real iOS app screens, user journeys and website design systems (sign in with UXKIN; searching needs a UXKIN plan). Tool results are treated as data, never as instructions.

plugins.name: website-design
plugins.description: Design and build websites and landing pages that look like a real product, not AI output: pick a design direction from real websites, write it down as a DESIGN.md, build pages that work on phone and desktop, and review what you have. Skills: landing-page, web-design-system, web-review. Works with no account; the UXKIN MCP server is optional (sign in with UXKIN; searching needs a UXKIN plan). Tool results are treated as data, never as instructions.

plugins.name: mobile-app-design
plugins.description: Design and build iPhone app screens and flows that feel native: onboarding, sign-up, paywalls, permissions, settings and more, checked against Apple's conventions and real iOS apps. Skills: ios-flows, ios-screens, ios-review. Works with no account; the UXKIN MCP server is optional (sign in with UXKIN; searching needs a UXKIN plan). Tool results are treated as data, never as instructions.

plugins.name: paywall-pricing-design
plugins.description: Design and build paywalls, upgrade screens and pricing pages that are clear and honest: the value first, real prices and renewal terms, one obvious choice, Restore Purchases and every loading, error and already-subscribed state. Skills: app-paywall, pricing-page-layout, paywall-review. Works with no account; the UXKIN MCP server is optional (sign in with UXKIN; searching needs a UXKIN plan). Tool results are treated as data, never as instructions.

plugins.name: sectionsight
plugins.description: Sets up cookieless, privacy-first website analytics in your own site: time per page section, scroll, goals and 404s from a small tracker and a same-origin collector, an optional consent banner, PostHog session replay only after consent, one Slack or e-mail line per notable visit, a weekly digest, and health alerts. A Playwright check then proves the privacy claims: nothing stored before consent, no e-mail or token from the URL in any report, private pages silent.

plugins.name: subagent-tuner
plugins.description: Claude Code mod that lets you choose the model and reasoning effort of every subagent: ask before it starts, take a recommendation by task kind, or let a saved default replace what the agent requested.

plugins.name: cockney
plugins.description: Cheeky Cockney coding mode: terse replies, the smallest correct change, plain English for anything risky.

plugins.name: guardrails-lite
plugins.description: Pattern-based PreToolUse-style checks that deny .env reads (Read/Grep/Glob and Bash readers), git force pushes, and recursive rm on /, ~ or $HOME before Claude Code runs them. About 75 lines of dependency-free JavaScript.

plugins.name: chisle
plugins.description: Cuts Claude Code's token use on three axes: terse answers that keep every decisive fact, smallest-code-that-works rules, and a PostToolUse hook that trims oversized tool output before it re-enters the context. Benchmarks with raw transcripts, including the runs it loses, are published in the repository.

plugins.name: moltnode
plugins.description: MoltNode by Chord: two hosted MCP servers and three skills, no API key. MoltNode reads 31 blockchains over JSON-RPC; Chord returns best-route DEX swap quotes and unsigned swap transactions (with the approval and a simulation) on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Monad, Robinhood Chain and Arc, plus token boards, candles, wallet PnL and smart money. Non-custodial: the user's own wallet signs every transaction, after the user confirms the quote in a later message. Skills: moltnode (reads and swaps end to end), chord (trading and market data), chord-charts (candlestick SVG charts for tokens on 8 EVM chains and Solana).

plugins.name: lead-finder
plugins.description: Finds B2B companies that fit your ideal customer and show a buying signal now, with a source link and an exact quote for every claim. Anything it can't check stays "unknown" instead of being guessed. A deterministic, standard-library Python script does the scoring, and hiring is checked on 7 public job-board APIs (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Recruitee, Breezy HR, Personio). No API keys.

plugins.name: akc-cycle
plugins.description: Audit and upkeep skills that keep the rules and skills in a Claude Code setup from piling up and going stale. Ask "audit my skills" and skill-stocktake proposes keep, merge or retire for each skill with a reason; the audit skills change a file only after you confirm it. Skills only: no hooks, no MCP servers, no settings. plugins.name: 041-planning-plan-mode

plugins.name: 042-planning-openspec

plugins.name: 110-java-maven-best-practices
plugins.description: Use when you need to review, improve, or troubleshoot a Maven pom.xml file — including dependency management with BOMs, plugin configuration, version centralization, multi-module project structure, build profiles, or any situation where you want to align your Maven setup with industry best practices.

plugins.name: 111-java-maven-dependencies
plugins.description: Use when you need to add or evaluate Maven dependencies that improve code quality — including nullness annotations (JSpecify), static analysis (Error Prone + NullAway), functional programming (VAVR), or architecture testing (ArchUnit) — and want a consultative, question-driven approach that adds only what you actually need.

plugins.name: 112-java-maven-plugins
plugins.description: Use when you need to add or configure Maven plugins in your pom.xml — including quality tools (enforcer, surefire, failsafe, jacoco, pitest, spotbugs, pmd), security scanning (OWASP), code formatting (Spotless), version management, container image build (Jib), build information tracking, and benchmarking (JMH) — through a consultative, modular step-by-step approach that only adds what you actually need.

plugins.name: 113-java-maven-documentation
plugins.description: Use when you need to create a DEVELOPER.md file for a Maven project — combining a fixed base template with dynamic sections derived from the project pom.xml, including a Plugin Goals Reference, Maven Profiles table, and Submodules table for multi-module projects.

plugins.name: 114-java-maven-search
plugins.description: Covers Maven Central search (Search API, maven-metadata.xml, artifact URLs) and project-local update reports via versions-maven-plugin (display-property-updates, display-dependency-updates, display-plugin-updates). Use when finding or verifying coordinates, browsing Central, or checking what newer versions apply to the user’s pom.xml.

plugins.name: 121-java-object-oriented-design
plugins.description: Use when you need to review, improve, or refactor Java code for object-oriented design quality — including applying SOLID, DRY, and YAGNI principles, improving class and interface design, fixing OOP concept misuse (encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism), identifying and resolving code smells (God Class, Feature Envy, Data Clumps), or improving object creation patterns, method design, and exception handling.

plugins.name: 122-java-type-design
plugins.description: Use when you need to review, improve, or refactor Java code for type design quality — including establishing clear type hierarchies, applying consistent naming conventions, eliminating primitive obsession with domain-specific value objects, leveraging generic type parameters, creating type-safe wrappers, designing fluent interfaces, ensuring precision-appropriate numeric types (BigDecimal for financial calculations), and improving type contrast through interfaces and method signature alignment.

plugins.name: 124-java-secure-coding
plugins.description: Use when you need to apply Java secure coding best practices — including validating untrusted inputs, defending against injection attacks with parameterized queries, minimizing attack surface via least privilege, applying strong cryptographic algorithms, handling exceptions securely without exposing sensitive data, managing secrets at runtime, avoiding unsafe deserialization, and encoding output to prevent XSS.

plugins.name: 125-java-concurrency
plugins.description: Use when you need to apply Java concurrency best practices — including thread safety fundamentals, ExecutorService thread pool management, concurrent design patterns like Producer-Consumer, asynchronous programming with CompletableFuture, immutability and safe publication, deadlock avoidance, virtual threads, scoped values, backpressure, cancellation discipline, and observability for concurrent systems.

plugins.name: 126-java-exception-handling
plugins.description: Use when you need to apply Java exception handling best practices — including using specific exception types, managing resources with try-with-resources, securing exception messages, preserving error context via exception chaining, validating inputs early with fail-fast principles, handling thread interruption correctly, documenting exceptions with @throws, enforcing logging policy, translating exceptions at API boundaries, managing retries and idempotency, enforcing timeouts, attaching suppressed exceptions, and propagating failures in async/reactive code.

plugins.name: 181-java-observability-logging
plugins.description: Use when you need to implement or improve Java logging and observability — including selecting SLF4J with Logback/Log4j2, applying proper log levels (ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE), parameterized logging, secure logging without sensitive data exposure, environment-specific configuration, log aggregation and monitoring, or validating logging through tests.

plugins.name: 182-java-observability-metrics-micrometer
plugins.description: Use when you need to implement or improve Java metrics observability with Micrometer — including meter design, naming/tag conventions, cardinality control, timers/counters/gauges/distribution summaries, percentiles/histograms, Actuator/Prometheus integration, and metrics validation through tests.

plugins.name: 183-java-observability-tracing-opentelemetry
plugins.description: Use when you need to implement or improve distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry in Java — including trace/span modeling, context propagation, semantic conventions, span attributes/events/status, sampling strategy, baggage usage, privacy safeguards, and backend integration with OTLP collectors.

plugins.name: 128-java-generics
plugins.description: Use when you need to review, improve, or refactor Java code for generics quality — including avoiding raw types, applying the PECS (Producer Extends Consumer Super) principle for wildcards, using bounded type parameters, designing effective generic methods, leveraging the diamond operator, understanding type erasure implications, handling generic inheritance correctly, preventing heap pollution with @SafeVarargs, and integrating generics with modern Java features like Records, sealed types, and pattern matching.

plugins.name: 130-java-testing-strategies
plugins.description: Use when you need to apply testing strategies for Java code — RIGHT-BICEP to guide test creation, A-TRIP for test quality characteristics, or CORRECT for verifying boundary conditions.

plugins.name: 131-java-testing-unit-testing
plugins.description: Use when you need to review, improve, or write Java unit tests — including migrating from JUnit 4 to JUnit 5, adopting AssertJ for fluent assertions, structuring tests with Given-When-Then, ensuring test independence, applying parameterized tests, mocking dependencies with Mockito, verifying boundary conditions (RIGHT-BICEP, CORRECT, A-TRIP), leveraging JSpecify null-safety annotations, or eliminating testing anti-patterns such as reflection-based tests or shared mutable state.

plugins.name: 132-java-testing-integration-testing
plugins.description: Use when you need to set up, review, or improve Java integration tests — including generating a BaseIntegrationTest.java with WireMock for HTTP stubs, detecting HTTP client infrastructure from import signals, injecting service coordinates dynamically via System.setProperty(), creating WireMock JSON mapping files with bodyFileName, isolating stubs per test method, verifying HTTP interactions, or eliminating anti-patterns such as Mockito-mocked HTTP clients or globally registered WireMock stubs.

plugins.name: 133-java-testing-acceptance-tests
plugins.description: Use when you need to implement acceptance tests from a Gherkin .feature file for framework-agnostic Java (no Spring Boot, Quarkus, Micronaut) — finding @acceptance scenarios, happy path with RestAssured, Testcontainers for DB/Kafka, WireMock for external REST. Requires .feature file in context.

plugins.name: 141-java-refactoring-with-modern-features
plugins.description: Use when you need to refactor Java code to adopt modern Java features (Java 8+) — including migrating anonymous classes to lambdas, replacing Iterator loops with Stream API, adopting Optional for null safety, switching from legacy Date/Calendar to java.time, using collection factory methods, applying text blocks, var inference, or leveraging Java 25 features like flexible constructor bodies and module import declarations.

plugins.name: 142-java-functional-programming
plugins.description: Use when you need to apply functional programming principles in Java — including writing immutable objects and Records, pure functions, functional interfaces, lambda expressions, Stream API pipelines, Optional for null safety, function composition, higher-order functions, pattern matching for instanceof and switch, sealed classes/interfaces for controlled hierarchies, Stream Gatherers for custom operations, currying/partial application, effect boundary separation, and concurrent-safe functional patterns.

plugins.name: 143-java-functional-exception-handling
plugins.description: Use when you need to apply functional exception handling best practices in Java — including replacing exception overuse with Optional and VAVR Either types, designing error type hierarchies using sealed classes and enums, implementing monadic error composition pipelines, establishing functional control flow patterns, and reserving exceptions only for truly exceptional system-level failures.

plugins.name: 144-java-data-oriented-programming
plugins.description: Use when you need to apply data-oriented programming best practices in Java — including separating code (behavior) from data structures using records, designing immutable data with pure transformation functions, keeping data flat and denormalized with ID-based references, starting with generic data structures converting to specific types when needed, ensuring data integrity through pure validation functions, and creating flexible generic data access layers.

plugins.name: 151-java-performance-jmeter

plugins.name: 161-java-profiling-detect

plugins.name: 162-java-profiling-analyze

plugins.name: 163-java-profiling-refactor

plugins.name: 164-java-profiling-verify
plugins.description: Use when you need to verify Java performance optimizations by comparing profiling results before and after refactoring — including baseline validation, post-refactoring report generation, quantitative before/after metrics comparison, side-by-side flamegraph analysis, regression detection, or creating profiling-comparison-analysis and profiling-final-results documentation.

plugins.name: 170-java-documentation
plugins.description: Use when you need to generate or improve Java project documentation — including README.md files, package-info.java files, and Javadoc enhancements — through a modular, step-based interactive process that adapts to your specific documentation needs.

plugins.name: 200-agents-md

plugins.name: 311-frameworks-spring-jdbc

plugins.name: 312-frameworks-spring-data-jdbc
plugins.description: Use when you need to use Spring Data JDBC with Java records — including entity design with records, repository pattern, immutable updates, aggregate relationships, custom queries, transaction management, and avoiding N+1 problems.

plugins.name: 321-frameworks-spring-boot-testing-unit-tests

plugins.name: 322-frameworks-spring-boot-testing-integration-tests
plugins.description: Use when you need to write or improve integration tests — including Testcontainers with @ServiceConnection, @DataJdbcTest persistence slices, TestRestTemplate or MockMvcTester for HTTP, data isolation, and container lifecycle management for Spring Boot 4.0.x.

plugins.name: 323-frameworks-spring-boot-testing-acceptance-tests

plugins.name: 402-frameworks-quarkus-rest
plugins.description: Use when you need to design, review, or improve REST APIs with Quarkus REST (Jakarta REST) — including resource classes, HTTP methods, status codes, request/response DTOs, Bean Validation, exception mappers, optional runtime OpenAPI exposure (SmallRye), contract-first generation from OpenAPI, content negotiation, pagination, sorting and filtering, API versioning, idempotency (Idempotency-Key), optimistic concurrency (ETag / If-Match), HTTP caching (Cache-Control), API deprecation (Sunset / Deprecation headers), RFC 7807 Problem Details, ISO-8601 for time in contracts, and security-aware boundaries.

plugins.name: 411-frameworks-quarkus-jdbc

plugins.name: 412-frameworks-quarkus-panache
plugins.description: Use when you need data access with Quarkus Hibernate ORM Panache — including PanacheEntity / PanacheEntityBase, PanacheRepository, named queries, JPQL, native SQL, DTO projections (project(Class)), pagination (Page.of()), N+1 avoidance (JOIN FETCH), optimistic locking (@Version / OptimisticLockException), @NamedQuery for validated reusable queries, transactions, @TestTransaction for test isolation, and immutable-friendly patterns. plugins.name: 413-frameworks-quarkus-db-migrations-flyway
plugins.description: Use when you need to add or review Flyway database migrations in a Quarkus application — quarkus-flyway extension, db/migration scripts, quarkus.flyway.* configuration, migrate-at-start, and alignment with JDBC or Panache.

plugins.name: 421-frameworks-quarkus-testing-unit-tests

plugins.name: 422-frameworks-quarkus-testing-integration-tests

plugins.name: 423-frameworks-quarkus-testing-acceptance-tests
plugins.description: Use when you need to implement acceptance tests from a Gherkin .feature file for Quarkus applications — including @acceptance scenarios, @QuarkusTest, BaseAcceptanceTest with QuarkusTestResourceLifecycleManager for Testcontainers and WireMock, REST Assured for full HTTP pipeline testing, WireMock JSON mapping files (classpath:wiremock/mappings/), *AT suffix naming, and Maven Surefire/Failsafe three-tier split. Requires the .feature file in context.

plugins.name: 502-frameworks-micronaut-rest
plugins.description: Use when you need to design, review, or improve REST APIs with Micronaut — including @Controller routes, HTTP status codes, DTOs, Bean Validation, exception handlers, pagination, idempotency, ETag/If-Match, caching headers, versioning, contract-first OpenAPI (OpenAPI Generator), optional runtime OpenAPI via micronaut-openapi, and security annotations.

plugins.name: 511-frameworks-micronaut-jdbc
plugins.description: Use when you need programmatic JDBC in Micronaut — pooled DataSource, parameterized SQL, io.micronaut.transaction.annotation.Transactional, batching, and domain exception translation.

plugins.name: 512-frameworks-micronaut-data

plugins.name: 513-frameworks-micronaut-db-migrations-flyway

plugins.name: 523-frameworks-micronaut-testing-acceptance-tests

Requires the .feature file in context.

plugins.name: agent-radar
plugins.description: One live line above the prompt per running subagent or background shell: its model, time, tool count and what it's doing. /radar shows every agent and its messages.

plugins.name: blast-radius-hamzafer
plugins.description: Holds risky Bash commands and shows what they would change before they run.

plugins.name: secret-guard
plugins.description: Keeps API keys and tokens out of Claude's context, your files and your commits: hides them in tool output, and asks before a write, commit or push adds one.

plugins.name: context-bar
plugins.description: Your context window as a stacked bar above the prompt, a color per category, with token counts and the compaction point. /context-bar shows or hides it.

plugins.name: browser-lanes
plugins.description: Shows if this session has a Playwright browser and who holds it. /browser clean closes leftover browsers. A subagent that wants the browser waits until the one using it is done.

plugins.name: md-preview
plugins.description: Shows the Markdown files Claude edits, rendered like GitHub, in a pane next to the chat. Before and after side by side. /md opens it.

plugins.name: glance
plugins.description: One line above the prompt with what needs you: next meeting, PRs, Linear issues and Slack DMs. /glance lists them all.

plugins.name: heatmap
plugins.description: A GitHub-style grid of your Claude Code time in a /heatmap pane, with streaks, peaks and top projects.

plugins.name: merge-gate
plugins.description: Holds `gh pr merge` until CI passes and one Codex review (OpenAI's luna model) has run. A PR line above the prompt, and /gate shows the PR's status.

plugins.name: mission-control-hamzafer
plugins.description: /mission opens a live map of the main agent, its subagents and every tool call, plus a code map of the files they touch.

plugins.name: next-steps
plugins.description: After each turn, 2 or 3 likely next prompts above the prompt. Press 1, 2 or 3 in an empty prompt to draft one, 0 to dismiss.

plugins.name: now-playing
plugins.description: What Spotify is playing, one line above the prompt: track, progress and the lyric being sung, with ⏮ ⏸ ⏭ buttons. /music controls it too. macOS.

plugins.name: prayer-times
plugins.description: The current prayer and how long is left, the next prayer, and zawal, above the prompt. Computed on your computer from your location; nothing is sent anywhere.

plugins.name: reels
plugins.description: YouTube Shorts in a terminal pane: plays while Claude works, pauses when Claude is done.

plugins.name: replay-theater
plugins.description: Step through the last turn's file edits, one diff at a time.

plugins.name: review-watch
plugins.description: A live line above the prompt for each running code review: Codex or a review subagent, its model, what it reviews, time, and Codex's latest output. A toast with the findings when it ends.

plugins.name: rulebook-guard
plugins.description: Writing and git rules: replaces em dashes in prose, and asks before git commit --amend, an unformatted push, or personal info in notes and commits.

plugins.name: session-saver
plugins.description: Names untitled sessions through unpause. /park saves where you left off, and a resumed session shows it.

plugins.name: snake
plugins.description: Snake in a pane while Claude works, paused when it's done. Opt-in, so nothing opens until /snake.

plugins.name: token-weather
plugins.description: A live forecast of the context window, with a prompt-cache countdown, drawn above the prompt.

plugins.name: cache-clock

plugins.description: Meta-plugin that installs the bundled Han suite. Has no components of its own; it depends on han-communication, han-core, han-documentation, han-research, han-planning, han-coding, han-github, and han-reporting so installing it pulls them all in. Does not bundle the opt-in han-feedback, han-atlassian, or han-plugin-builder plugins.

plugins.name: han-communication
plugins.description: Foundational communication plugin for the Han suite. Owns the canonical readability standard, writing-voice profile, and explanation standard, the readability-guidance skill that surfaces the first two into a calling skill's context for in-voice drafting, the explanation-guidance skill that surfaces the third at the point a run talks to a person, the readability-editor agent that runs the adversarial rewrite, and the edit-for-readability skill. Depends on nothing and sits beneath every other plugin; the plugins that produce prose output depend on it.

plugins.name: han-core
plugins.description: The shared foundation of the Han suite: the specialist agent roster the other plugins dispatch, the project-discovery skill with its project-scanner agent, and the canonical evidence and YAGNI rule files. The documentation skills live in han-documentation, the pre-planning research skills in han-research, the planning skills in han-planning, and the coding skills in han-coding; each depends on han-core.

plugins.name: han-documentation
plugins.description: Documentation skills for the Han suite: writing down what the team built and decided. Home of project-documentation, architectural-decision-record, and runbook. Depends on han-communication and han-core; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-research
plugins.description: Pre-planning knowledge-work skills for the Han suite: understanding a problem before anyone commits to a plan. Home of research, gap-analysis, and issue-triage, plus the research-analyst agent. Depends on han-communication and han-core; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-planning
plugins.description: Planning skills for the Han suite: specifying, planning, sequencing, breaking down, and stress-testing work before implementation. Home of plan-a-feature, plan-implementation, plan-a-phased-build, plan-work-items, and iterative-plan-review, plus the discussion-facilitator agent. Depends on han-communication and han-core; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-coding
plugins.description: Code-writing and execution skills for the Han suite. Home of the tdd skill, which drives a feature or behavior through a BDD-framed red-green-refactor loop with an enforced observed-failure gate. Depends on han-core and han-communication; bundled by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-github
plugins.description: GitHub-specific extensions to Han. Provides skills to post code reviews as PR comments, update a PR description with a consistent format, and other GitHub-facing workflows.

plugins.name: han-reporting
plugins.description: Reporting and summary skills for the Han suite. Turns feature specifications into plain-language stakeholder summaries (also called executive or business summaries) with diagrams, for sharing with non-technical stakeholders before implementation kicks off.

plugins.name: han-feedback
plugins.description: Post-session feedback skill for the Han suite. Captures structured observations, ratings, and improvement ideas on the Han skills you ran in a session and optionally posts them as a GitHub issue to testdouble/han. Opt-in: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-atlassian
plugins.description: Atlassian-facing extensions to the Han suite. Adds markdown-to-confluence, which publishes a local Markdown file to a user-specified Confluence page; project-documentation-to-confluence, which runs the han-documentation project-documentation skill and then publishes the result there; investigate-to-confluence, which runs the core investigate skill and publishes the resulting investigation report there; code-overview-to-confluence, which runs the core code-overview skill and publishes the resulting overview there; plan-a-feature-to-confluence, which runs the core plan-a-feature skill and publishes the spec and its companion artifacts there as a page tree; and work-items-to-jira, which creates one Jira ticket per slice from a work-items file. All work through the Atlassian MCP server. Depends on han-core, han-documentation, han-planning, and han-coding (its wrapper skills run skills from each and its wrapped skills dispatch the shared han-core agents), and on han-communication (its wrapped prose-producing skills source the shared readability standard), and requires a configured Atlassian MCP server. Opt-in: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-linear
plugins.description: Linear-facing extensions to the Han suite. Adds work-items-to-linear, which creates one Linear issue per slice from a work-items file. Works through the Linear MCP server and requires it to be configured. Depends on no other Han plugin. Opt-in: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

plugins.name: han-ddd
plugins.description: Strategic Domain-Driven Design analysis for the Han suite. Discovers domain boundaries, identifies bounded context candidates (strongly expressed, latent, and speculative), finds boundary leaks, and produces an evidence-backed domain and context map for an existing codebase. Depends on han-communication and han-core. Opt-in: not bundled by the han meta-plugin.

Opt-in and dependency-free: installed on its own, not pulled in by the han meta-plugin.

Draft, then run this pass on the draft before handing it over. Also use when someone says "de-claude", "de-slop", "humanize this", "this reads like AI", "make it sound human", or asks for a voice, tone or register edit. Rewrites the constructions that mark prose as model-written (staged reveals, verdict headers, aphoristic closers, "it's not X, it's Y", em-dash drama, forced triads, flat-certainty adverbs, noun stacks, dropped 'that') into plain technical prose and checks the rewrite kept every claim. plugins.name: diagnostic-legibility
plugins.description: Agents accountable for helping to maintain human understanding. Ships the `diagnostic-legibility` agent — builds and self-challenges two models of a codebase scope (architectural moving parts and domain concepts) via a five-question retained-challenge cycle, then cross-checks the two collections against each other via a five-question per-direction cycle. The `/diagnose` command surfaces the mutually-corrected models on demand as a readable report. The `ConceptualPipelineMap` template adds a standalone, presentation-agnostic flow-perspective data model; the agent's `scope-resolution` mode answers 'what does my task touch?' (a bounded, disclosed scope from a work task); and its `pipeline` mode traces control flow within that bound into a ConceptualPipelineMap alongside the architectural/domain collections, then cross-checks all three against each other (the maximal six directed pairs) for mutual correction. The `/pipeline-map "<task>"` command renders the task-scoped map as a self-contained HTML flowchart (pinned, SHA-verified Mermaid inlined; no CDN) with a scope-resolution panel, node-detail table, and no-JS fallback; `--predict-change` adds an opt-in change-site prediction (which stages the task will modify and where it will insert new ones) disclosed as a prediction, never a directive.

plugins.name: guardrails-fvadicamo
plugins.description: Safety guardrails for running Claude Code with reduced supervision. The guard-destructive PreToolUse hook matches against a normalized view of each command (heredoc bodies and comments stripped, quoted strings neutralized except interpreter arguments like ssh / sh -c / eval / su / doas), so a command that merely mentions a destructive pattern is not flagged. It hard-blocks catastrophic Bash commands (rm -rf /, rsync --delete, docker volume rm) and makes rm/rmdir scope-aware: operations whose operands all resolve inside the allowed workspace (the session project root, temp dirs, any $GUARD_ALLOWED_EXTRA root, or a variable assigned from a bare mktemp earlier in the same command) run silently, while anything outside it (or any glob/variable/escape it cannot resolve) raises a single reflective confirmation. git reset --hard / clean / restore, shred, dd, mkfs still always prompt.

The denylist is never committed, so the hook is a no-op for external contributors and in CI while gitleaks still covers generic secrets.

plugins.name: decision-records
plugins.description: Creates, supersedes and validates decision records (ADRs) against the convention a collection already follows, instead of against a published spec it may never have adopted. Ships the decision-records skill: a propose-then-write flow that never rewrites an accepted record, and check-decisions.sh, a validator that deduces the filename scheme, section set and status vocabulary from the records already present and reports eight classes of violation with a stable code and an exit status. Ships no template into the target repo, and delegates private-token scanning to privacy-guard rather than keeping a second denylist.

plugins.description: Deutsches Straßenverkehrsrecht in drei Säulen: zivilrechtliche Haftung (StVG §§ 7, 17, 18; BGB §§ 823, 249–254) mit Quotenrechtsprechung und Schadensposten, verwaltungsrechtliche Fahreignungsprüfung (FeV §§ 11, 13, 14, 46; MPU-Anordnung; § 80 V VwGO), Verkehrs-OWi (StVO, BKatV, OWiG §§ 67, 71) und Schnittstelle Verkehrsstrafrecht §§ 142, 315c, 316 StGB.

plugins.name: transportrecht
plugins.description: Deutsches Transportrecht – HGB-Frachtführerhaftung §§ 407–452d (Obhutshaftung § 425, Begrenzung § 431 mit 8,33 SZR/kg, qualifiziertes Verschulden § 435, Schadensanzeige § 438, Verjährung § 439), CMR für grenzüberschreitenden Straßengüterverkehr (Art. 17, 23, 29, 30, 31, 32), Speditionsvertrag §§ 453 ff. HGB, ADSp 2017 als AGB.

plugins.name: produktrecht
plugins.description: Deutsches Produktrecht – verschuldensunabhängige Herstellerhaftung nach ProdHaftG und Produzentenhaftung § 823 BGB (Konstruktions-, Fabrikations-, Instruktions-, Produktbeobachtungsfehler), Produktsicherheit GPSR (VO (EU) 2023/988) mit ProdSG-Übergang und sektoraler Harmonisierung, Rückrufrecht zivil- und öffentlich-rechtlich (Marktaufsicht der Länder, BAuA, Safety Business Gateway).

plugins.name: ki-governance-borghei
plugins.description: KI-Governance als Querschnittsdisziplin – Aufbau- und Ablauforganisation für den KI-Einsatz, Rollen, Lieferantenmanagement (AVV Art. 28 DSGVO, § 43e BRAO), Ethik-Leitplanken, ISO/IEC 42001 / 23894, NIST AI RMF, BSI AIC4. Skills: KI-Risikoassessment, KI-Monitoring-Konzept, KI-Richtlinien-Entwurf. Gesetzliche KI-VO-Pflichten siehe Plugin ki-vo-compliance.

plugins.name: patentrecht
plugins.description: Deutsches und europäisches Patentrecht – Patentanmeldung und Vorprüfung nach PatG/EPÜ (technischer Charakter, Neuheit § 3 PatG / Art. 54 EPÜ, erfinderische Tätigkeit § 4 PatG / Art. 56 EPÜ, Aufgabe-Lösungs-Ansatz), Patentverletzungsklage §§ 9, 14, 139 ff. PatG (Düsseldorfer Modell, dreifache Schadensberechnung, Äquivalenz), Freedom-to-Operate. Hinweise auf GebrMG, ArbnErfG, Einheitspatent/UPC.

plugins.name: migrationsrecht
plugins.description: Deutsches Migrations- und Asylrecht – Aufenthaltstitel-Systematik nach AufenthG (Erteilungsvoraussetzungen § 5, Erwerb/Studium/Familiennachzug/humanitäre Titel, Chancen-Aufenthalt § 25c), Asylantrag und BAMF-Verfahren nach AsylG (§§ 3, 4, 60 V/VII AufenthG, Dublin-VO 604/2013, Folgeantrag § 71), Abschiebungsschutz und Eilrechtsschutz (§ 80 V VwGO, § 36 III AsylG, Duldung § 60a).

plugins.name: agrarrecht
plugins.description: Deutsches Agrarrecht – GAP-Förderantrag 2023–2027 (VO (EU) 2021/2115, GAP-DZG, GAPInVeKoSG, GAP-KondV, Öko-Regelungen, GLÖZ/GAB-Konditionalität), Grundstücksverkehrsrecht (GrdstVG-Genehmigung, RSG-Siedlungsvorkaufsrecht, LPachtVG-Anzeige), LwAnpG-Vermögensauseinandersetzung der LPG-Nachfolgegesellschaften vor dem Landwirtschaftsgericht.

plugins.name: sportrecht
plugins.description: Deutsches Sportrecht – Verbands- und Vereinsrecht (BGB §§ 21 ff.), Verbands- und Schiedsgerichtsbarkeit (CAS Lausanne, DIS, Pechstein-Linie), Anti-Doping (WADC, NADC, AntiDopG §§ 2–4), Athletenrecht (Spielerarbeitsvertrag, Persönlichkeitsrecht KUG, Vermarktung), Stadionverbot, Schnittstellen Bosman/Meca-Medina und Sportwetten.

plugins.name: urheber-medienrecht
plugins.description: Deutsches Urheber- und Medienrecht – Urheberrechtsverletzung mit § 97a UrhG-Abmahnung und dreifacher Schadensberechnung, Lizenzvertrag mit Zweckübertragungslehre und angemessener Vergütung §§ 32, 32a UrhG, medienrechtliche Pflichtenprüfung nach MStV (Impressum § 18, Trennungsgebot, journalistisch-redaktionelle Sorgfalt, Gegendarstellung). Schnittstellen UrhDaG, VGG, DSA, Landespressegesetze.

plugins.name: berufsrecht-anwaltschaft
plugins.description: Anwaltliches Berufsrecht – BRAO-Grundpflichtenprüfung (Verschwiegenheit § 43a II + § 203 StGB, Interessenkollision § 43a IV, Sachlichkeit § 43a III/§ 44, Werbung § 43b/§§ 6 ff. BORA, Auslagerung/KI § 43e, Vergütung § 49b, Fremdgeld § 43a V), FAO-Fortbildungsnachweis § 15 FAO inkl. Widerrufsverteidigung § 25 FAO, RDG-Abgrenzung (§§ 1, 2, 5, 10 RDG, Inkasso, Legal-Tech).

plugins.name: kapitalmarktrecht
plugins.description: Deutsches Kapitalmarktrecht im engeren Sinne – WpHG/MAR (Marktmissbrauch, Insiderhandel, Ad-hoc-Publizität, Directors' Dealings, Stimmrechtsmeldungen), Prospekt-VO (EU) 2017/1129 iVm WpPG (Prospektpflicht, Ausnahmen, BaFin-Billigung, Prospekthaftung), WpÜG (Pflichtangebot, Acting in concert, Mindestpreis, Verhaltenspflichten Zielgesellschaft, Squeeze-out).

plugins.name: kartellrecht
plugins.description: Deutsches und EU-Kartellrecht – GWB Teile 1–3 (Kartellverbot § 1, Marktbeherrschung §§ 18 ff., Fusionskontrolle §§ 35 ff.) inkl. § 19a strukturmarktrelevante Unternehmen sowie Art. 101/102 AEUV und EU-FK-VO 139/2004. GWB-Zusammenschlussanmeldung mit Vollzugsverbot § 41, Kartellverbots-Prüfung inkl. Vertikal-GVO 2022/720, Marktbeherrschung und Missbrauchsbewertung.

plugins.name: wohnungseigentumsrecht
plugins.description: Wohnungseigentumsrecht (WEG) nach der WEMoG-Reform (seit 01.12.2020) – Beschlussanfechtung §§ 23, 44, 45 WEG (Anfechtungsklage gegen die Gemeinschaft der Wohnungseigentümer, Monatsfrist, Nichtigkeit vs. Anfechtbarkeit), Jahresabrechnung und Hausgeld § 28 WEG (Wirtschaftsplan, Abrechnungsspitze, Vermögensbericht), bauliche Veränderung §§ 20, 21 WEG (Gestattungsbeschluss, privilegierte Maßnahmen inkl. E-Mobilität und Steckersolargeräte, Kostenverteilung), Eigentümerversammlung und virtuelle Versammlung § 23 Abs. 1a WEG, Verwalterbestellung und -abberufung §§ 26, 26a WEG, Änderung des Kostenverteilungsschlüssels § 16 Abs. 2 S. 2 WEG, Hausgeldbeitreibung und Entziehung §§ 17, 19, 28 WEG, Beschlussersetzungsklage § 44 Abs. 1 S. 2 WEG, vermietete Eigentumswohnung. Rechtsstand Oktober 2026.

plugins.name: cyber-resilience-act
plugins.description: EU Cyber Resilience Act – VO (EU) 2024/2847. Anwendungsbereichsprüfung (Produkt mit digitalen Elementen, Ausnahmen Art. 2, Rollenbestimmung, Verwalter quelloffener Software, Einstufung nach Anhang III/IV), Meldepflichten nach Art. 14 ab 11.09.2026 (24h-Frühwarnung, 72h-Vollmeldung, Abschlussbericht binnen 14 Tagen bzw. 1 Monat über die einheitliche Meldeplattform an CSIRT und ENISA), grundlegende Anforderungen nach Anhang I mit SBOM, Unterstützungszeitraum, technischer Dokumentation Anhang VII, Konformitätsbewertung Anhang VIII und CE-Kennzeichnung sowie koordinierte Schwachstellenoffenlegung und Schwachstellenmanagement.

plugins.name: immobilien-grundbuchrecht
plugins.description: Immobilien- und Grundbuchrecht. Grundstückskaufvertrag § 311b BGB, Auflassung § 925, GBO §§ 13/19/29/39, Grundschuld §§ 1191 ff., Teilungserklärung § 8 WEG.

plugins.name: zwangsvollstreckung
plugins.description: Zwangsvollstreckung / ZVG. Titel-Klausel-Zustellung §§ 704 ff. ZPO, PfÜB §§ 829/835, P-Konto § 850k, Vermögensauskunft § 802c, ZVG §§ 15/44/81/180.

plugins.name: kostenrecht-rvg
plugins.description: Kostenrecht (RVG / GKG / PKH). Gegenstandswert §§ 22 f. RVG, VV 2300/3100/3104, Kostenfestsetzung §§ 103 ff. ZPO, Vergütungsvereinbarung § 3a RVG, PKH §§ 114 ff. ZPO.

plugins.name: wirtschafts-steuerstrafrecht
plugins.description: Wirtschafts- und Steuerstrafrecht. § 370 AO, §§ 263/266/266a/299 StGB, Verbandsgeldbuße §§ 30/130 OWiG, Einziehung §§ 73 ff. StGB, Internal Investigations.

plugins.name: m-a-transaktionsrecht
plugins.description: M&A / Transaktionsrecht. Share Deal § 15 III/IV GmbHG, Garantien § 311 I BGB, Due Diligence, Asset Deal mit § 613a BGB und § 25 HGB.

plugins.name: vereins-stiftungs-gemeinnuetzigkeitsrecht
plugins.description: Vereins-, Stiftungs- und Gemeinnützigkeitsrecht. Verein §§ 21 ff. BGB, Stiftungsrecht §§ 80–88 BGB (Reform 2023), Gemeinnützigkeit §§ 51–68 AO, Spendenrecht § 10b EStG.

plugins.name: beamten-disziplinarrecht
plugins.description: Beamten- und Disziplinarrecht. Dienstvergehen § 47 BeamtStG, Disziplinarmaßnahmen §§ 5/13 BDG, Konkurrentenstreit Art. 33 II GG + § 123 VwGO, dienstliche Beurteilung.

plugins.name: reise-fluggastrecht
plugins.description: Reise- und Fluggastrecht. VO (EG) 261/2004 Art. 5/7/8/9, Pauschalreise §§ 651a ff. BGB, Rücktritt § 651h, Insolvenzabsicherung § 651r.

plugins.name: datenwirtschaftsrecht
plugins.description: Datenwirtschaftsrecht – EU-Datenverordnung (Data Act, VO (EU) 2023/2854) und ihre deutsche Durchführung im DADG. Anwendungsbereich und Rollen Art. 1, 2, 7, Geltungsbeginn 12.09.2025 / 12.09.2026 / 12.01.2027 Art. 50; Zugangsanspruch des Nutzers Art. 3, 4, 5, 6 mit Geschäftsgeheimnisschutz Art. 4 Abs. 6–8; B2B-Bereitstellung und angemessene Gegenleistung Art. 8, 9; Missbrauchskontrolle einseitig auferlegter Klauseln Art. 13 im Verhältnis zu §§ 305 ff. BGB; Anbieterwechsel bei Datenverarbeitungsdiensten Art. 23–31 mit Wegfall der Wechselentgelte ab 12.01.2027; Durchsetzung durch die Bundesnetzagentur §§ 2, 6–14 DADG und Bußgelder § 15 DADG. Abgrenzung zu DSGVO, GeschGehG und Datenbankschutz. Researcher/Drafter/Reviewer-Subagenten.

plugins.name: barrierefreiheit-bfsg
plugins.description: Barrierefreiheitsrecht – Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (BFSG) und BFSGV in Umsetzung der RL (EU) 2019/882, anwendbar seit dem 28.06.2025. Anwendungsbereich für Produkte § 1 Abs. 2 und Dienstleistungen § 1 Abs. 3, Kleinstunternehmensausnahme § 3 Abs. 3 iVm § 2 Nr. 17, Übergangsbestimmungen § 38; Pflichten von Hersteller, Einführer und Händler §§ 6–13 mit EU-Konformitätserklärung § 18 und CE-Kennzeichnung § 19; Pflichten des Dienstleistungserbringers § 14 mit Barrierefreiheitsinformationen nach Anlage 3 und den Anforderungen der §§ 12, 13, 19 BFSGV; Ausnahmen wegen grundlegender Veränderung § 16 und unverhältnismäßiger Belastung § 17 nebst Anlage 4; Marktüberwachung §§ 20–31, Verbraucher- und Verbandsrechte §§ 32–34, Bußgelder § 37. Abgrenzung zum Recht öffentlicher Stellen: BGG §§ 12a, 12b, 16 und BITV 2.0. Researcher/Drafter/Reviewer-Subagenten.

plugins.name: schiedsverfahren-adr
plugins.description: Schiedsverfahrensrecht und alternative Streitbeilegung – Zehntes Buch der ZPO §§ 1025–1066. Schiedsvereinbarung §§ 1029, 1030, 1031 mit Verbraucherform § 1031 Abs. 5, Einrede und Feststellungsantrag § 1032, Kompetenz-Kompetenz § 1040; Bildung und Ablehnung des Schiedsgerichts §§ 1034–1039, Verfahren §§ 1042–1050, einstweiliger Rechtsschutz §§ 1033, 1041, Kosten § 1057, Schiedsspruch §§ 1054, 1055; Aufhebungsantrag § 1059 mit Dreimonatsfrist und OLG-Zuständigkeit § 1062, Verfahren § 1063, Rechtsbeschwerde § 1065; Vollstreckbarerklärung inländischer § 1060 und ausländischer Schiedssprüche § 1061 iVm dem New Yorker Übereinkommen von 1958. Institutionelle Verfahren nach der DIS-Schiedsgerichtsordnung 2018 und Mediation nach dem MediationsG / § 278a ZPO. Researcher/Drafter/Reviewer-Subagenten.

plugins.name: gewerberecht
plugins.description: Gewerbe- und Handwerksrecht – Gewerbeordnung und Handwerksordnung in der Verwaltungspraxis. Gewerbeuntersagung wegen Unzuverlässigkeit § 35 GewO mit erweiterter Untersagung Abs. 1 S. 2, Sperrwirkung Abs. 8, Wiedergestattung Abs. 6 und Anhörung der Kammern Abs. 4; erlaubnispflichtige Gewerbe §§ 34a, 34c, 34d, 34f, 34i GewO nebst MaBV; Anzeigepflicht § 14 GewO und Verhinderung des Betriebs ohne Zulassung § 15 Abs. 2 GewO; Reisegewerbekarte §§ 55 ff. GewO, Anwendungsausnahmen § 6 GewO; Handwerksrolle §§ 1, 6–10 HwO, Meistervorbehalt Anlage A, Ausübungsberechtigung § 7b HwO, Ausnahmebewilligung § 8 HwO, EU/EWR § 9 HwO, Untersagung § 16 Abs. 3 HwO. Verfahren nach VwVfG und VwGO einschließlich Sofortvollzug § 80 Abs. 2 S. 1 Nr. 4 VwGO. Researcher/Drafter/Reviewer-Subagenten.

plugins.name: verbandsklage-vdug
plugins.description: Verbandsklagerecht nach dem VDuG – Abhilfeklage § 14 mit Gleichartigkeitserfordernis § 15, Abhilfegrundurteil § 16, kollektivem Gesamtbetrag § 19 iVm § 287 ZPO und Abhilfeendurteil § 18 mit zulassungsfreier Revision; Musterfeststellungsklage § 41 und Bindungswirkung § 11 Abs. 3; Zulässigkeit §§ 1–8 mit klageberechtigten Stellen § 2, Verbraucherquorum von 50 Betroffenen § 4 Abs. 1, Verbot der Drittfinanzierung § 4 Abs. 2 und ausschließlicher OLG-Zuständigkeit § 3; Anmeldung zum Verbandsklageregister § 46 binnen drei Wochen nach Schluss der mündlichen Verhandlung ohne § 193 BGB, Sperrwirkungen §§ 8, 11 und Umsetzungsverfahren §§ 22–40 mit Sachwalter, Umsetzungsfonds § 25 und Widerspruchsverfahren § 28. Kleine Unternehmen gelten nach § 1 Abs. 2 als Verbraucher. Researcher/Drafter/Reviewer-Subagenten.

plugins.name: kritis-resilienz
plugins.description: Physische Resilienz kritischer Anlagen nach dem KRITIS-Dachgesetz in Umsetzung der RL (EU) 2022/2557 – Geltungsbereich und zehn Sektoren § 4 mit Bereichsausnahme für DORA-Finanzunternehmen § 4 Abs. 2, Erheblichkeitsschwellen § 5, Registrierung binnen drei Monaten § 8 über die gemeinsame Stelle von BSI und BBK, Risikoanalyse des Betreibers § 12, Resilienzpflichten und Resilienzplan § 13, Mindestanforderungen § 14, Nachweise und Audits § 16, Vorfallmeldung § 18 mit 24-Stunden-Erstmeldung und ausführlichem Bericht binnen eines Monats, Umsetzungs- und Überwachungspflicht der Geschäftsleitung § 20 nebst Haftung, Berichtspflichten § 21 und Bußgelder bis 1 Mio. EUR § 24. Zentrale Anlaufstelle ist das BBK, sektorspezifisch zuständig sind BNetzA, BMI, BMWE und weitere Behörden § 3. Abgrenzung zu NIS2/BSIG. Researcher/Drafter/Reviewer-Subagenten.

plugins.name: entgelttransparenz-eu
plugins.description: Entgelttransparenz nach der RL (EU) 2023/970 und dem EntgTranspG – Umsetzungsfrist 07.06.2026 von Deutschland versäumt, daher unmittelbare Wirkung gegenüber staatlichen Arbeitgebern, Staatshaftung nach Francovich und richtlinienkonforme Auslegung des geltenden EntgTranspG; Entgelttransparenz vor der Beschäftigung Art. 5 mit Verbot der Frage nach der Entgeltentwicklung, Auskunftsrecht Art. 7 mit Zweimonatsfrist und Unwirksamkeit von Verschwiegenheitsklauseln, Berichterstattung Art. 9 mit den Schwellen 250 / 150 / 100 Beschäftigte und den Stichtagen 07.06.2027 und 07.06.2031, gemeinsame Entgeltbewertung Art. 10 ab 5 Prozent unerklärtem Entgeltgefälle, Beweislastumkehr Art. 18 mit Vollumkehr bei Transparenzpflichtverletzungen, Verjährung von mindestens drei Jahren ab Kenntnis Art. 21, Schadensersatz Art. 16 und Kosten Art. 22. Researcher/Drafter/Reviewer-Subagenten.

plugins.name: krypto-mikar
plugins.description: Kryptowerteaufsicht nach der MiCAR (VO (EU) 2023/1114) und dem deutschen Kryptomärkteaufsichtsgesetz (KMAG) – Anwendungsbereich und Tokenklassen (vermögenswertreferenzierte Token, E-Geld-Token, sonstige Kryptowerte) mit den Ausnahmen des Art. 2 Abs. 3, 4 und der Abgrenzung zu KWG, WpIG, KAGB und ZAG; Kryptowerte-Whitepaper, öffentliches Angebot und Zulassung zum Handel nebst Haftung Art. 15 und § 19 KMAG; Zulassung und laufende Aufsicht der Anbieter von Kryptowerte-Dienstleistungen mit BaFin-Befugnissen §§ 3, 4, 9 bis 25 KMAG, digitaler operationaler Resilienz § 26 und Übergangsvorschrift § 50; Marktmissbrauchsregime Titel VI MiCAR mit Insiderhandel und Marktmanipulation, Verfolgung §§ 31 bis 36 KMAG, Straf- und Bußgeldvorschriften §§ 46, 47 KMAG. Researcher/Drafter/Reviewer-Subagenten.
